title: ADLC ticket
description: A stored ADLC ticket. `adlc ticket create` accepts the same document without `id`, which the store mints as a ULID.

id.description: Ticket id. Omit it on create and the store mints a ULID (T-01K...); supply one only to keep an existing T<n> id.

title.description: One imperative line naming the work.

body.description: The self-contained ticket text: what to build, the acceptance criteria, and the concrete command that verifies each one. A fresh agent sees only this — never the conversation that produced it. coldstart audits it for gaps.

category.description: Routing hint, not a free-form label. model-router sends contract, spec, and architecture to a frontier model and routes the rest from empirical priors. Keep to the set ticket-sync accepts or a synced ticket cannot converge: feature, bug, bugfix, refactor, docs, chore, test, spec, contract, architecture.

duration.description: Positive number (number > 0) giving the relative build-time estimate used to order the ticket DAG. Defaults to 1.

budget.description: Optional token ceiling. model-router and flail-detector honour a positive number and ignore anything else; the store does not validate it. Omit it to take the tier default.

scope.description: Path globs this ticket may touch, e.g. src/auth/**.

rails.description: Path globs frozen for the duration of the build; rails-guard denies edits to them. Each rail must match at least one file in the repository when it is added, or the write is refused (RAIL_MATCHES_NOTHING). Narrowing rails, widening scope, or changing `completed` on an existing ticket requires `--authorize` (see `adlc ticket update --help`); `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS` governs only the `rails-guard` hook/CLI check on direct store-path edits, not `adlc ticket` writes.

completed.description: Lifecycle state, set by `adlc ticket complete` rather than authored by hand. It is part of the stored document, so an update that omits it REMOVES it — build updates from `show <id> --json`, not from scratch.

to.description: Id of the dependent ticket (this ticket completes before `to`, which must not start before this one completes).

contract.description: Path to the interface this edge guarantees the dependent ticket can consume.

edges.description: Array of edge objects (each with a non-empty string "to" id) giving ordering constraints, prerequisite to dependent: this ticket completes before `to` (an edge with "to": "TX" on THIS ticket means this ticket must complete before TX — so making this ticket depend on an existing one is an edge added to that existing ticket, never a reversed edge here). An edge may also carry "contract": a path to the interface it guarantees TX can consume, which is what lets the two be built in parallel; ticket-sync recognizes it and nothing else on an edge.
